logseq-entity-hierarchy-type:: — how a child entity relates to its parent

This property says whether a child entity is a kind of its parent or a part of it, and it goes on the child's definition page, the one whose name nests under the parent's. Every blog post is an article, so the Logseq/Entity/Article/Blog definition page, which nests under Logseq/Entity/Article, would carry logseq-entity-hierarchy-type:: [[Logseq/Entity/Hierarchy/Frontmatter/Type/extends]].

logseq-entity-hierarchy-type:: — how a child entity relates to its parent

The child entity is a kind of its parent: every instance of the child is also an instance of the parent, and the child definition page states only how its instances differ from the parent's. Logseq/Entity/Person/Maker extends Logseq/Entity/Person, and Logseq/Entity/Article/Blog extends Logseq/Entity/Article.

The child entity is a different thing that belongs to an instance of its parent. An episode belongs to a show, so Logseq/Entity/Podcast/Episode is part of Logseq/Entity/Podcast, and one page is never both a show and one of its episodes. Whoever files a part-of instance usually puts its page under the page of the thing it belongs to, so an episode's page goes in its show's Pod namespace, as Hard Fork/Pod/26/09/A.I. Safety Goes Mainstream + a ‘Hard Fork’ Exit AMA sits under Hard Fork/Pod.
In this garden, Identity pages model a public name under which a person or collective publishes, performs or makes work.
A stage name, pen name, named artistic project or collective with a recognizable body of work. The identity has a page separate from the biographical people behind it.
A person's ordinary biographical name alone does not require a second page. A spelling variant or abbreviation that names the same identity can remain an alias.
A shared credit does not by itself establish a new collective identity. A collaboration can credit several existing identities.
Use the published name as a short page title, such as Bibio. Entity classification belongs in frontmatter, rather than in an Identity/ prefix on every instance.
Add a disambiguating namespace only when the published name collides with another page.
Mark an instance with its most specific identity entity; a Band instance leaves Identity and Music Identity out of logseq-entity::.
A person can have several identities, and a collective identity can have several people behind it. Identity pages carry identity entities; biographical pages carry person or maker entities.
Logseq/Entity/Identity/Frontmatter/identity-of links an identity to known people behind it. Unknown people are left unstated.
Logseq/Frontmatter/created-by-identities links a work or release to its credited identities. A link to an identity does not imply that every associated person contributed to every work.
A work's created-by:: links the known people who made that particular work. Identity membership alone is insufficient evidence for a personal credit.
Search published names, existing titles, aliases, official URLs and person-page mentions before creating an identity.

When the identity exists only as an alias on a person page, retain the biographical page and separate the identity from that alias before creating its page. Other aliases and the person's biographical information remain with the person.
Older pages under Group/ can already represent collective identities. Their existing titles remain valid until deliberately renamed.
One linked H1 with the published name and official URL when known, a short description, and verified links to the people behind the identity.
The shared attribution property is linked above; domain-specific placement of works and recordings is defined by the corresponding identity child and work entity.

In this garden, Music Identity pages model the public artist or project names under which music is released or performed.
Naming, person relationships, deduplication and marking follow Logseq/Entity/Identity. A Music Identity is an identity, not a biographical musician.
A recording's Logseq/Frontmatter/created-by-identities lists the identities credited on the release, in published order.
Place releases under the first credited identity as <Identity>/Music/Recording/<Title>, following Logseq/Entity/Music/Recording. A joint release has one page and lists every credited identity.

Place a separately represented composition under its primary credited identity as <Identity>/Music/Work/<Title>, following Logseq/Entity/Music/Work. A recording's artist credit does not establish the composition's authorship.
Personal credits still link the people who actually wrote, produced or performed the music, following Logseq/Entity/Person/Maker.
Bibio and Dorian Concept are solo music identities, each linked to a separate person hub.
Bibio/Music/Recording/Answers credits both identities without creating a separate identity for their collaboration.
In this garden, Band pages model music identities shared by musicians working as a named band.
Attribution and release placement follow Logseq/Entity/Identity/Music, which inherits Logseq/Entity/Identity. A Band instance carries only the Band entity from this lineage.
A band's identity and release namespace persist through changes of membership. Albums belong under the band, rather than under an individual member.

Known people can be linked through Logseq/Entity/Identity/Frontmatter/identity-of. Membership periods, instruments and roles belong in dated body blocks when known; an undated person link makes no claim about current membership.
A recording lists individual participants only when their participation on that recording is known. Neither a current nor a historical membership list establishes a recording credit.
A one-off joint credit is not automatically a band. A named project receives a Band page when it has a band identity of its own.

In this garden, Key pages model a single physical or logical Keyboard/Computer key. These pages are anchor points for expressing Keyshorts along with some optional historical commentary on certain special computer keyboard keys.
Future instances: Key/Control, Key/Shift, Key/Command, Key/Option, Key/Escape, Key/Return, Key/Tab
